pack: S3 — Marshall Islands — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (MH)

results.raw: False. The Marshall Islands Judiciary does not publish case decisions; official reports are issued by the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute (PacLII).
False. No such General Order 2005-001 appears in the Marshall Islands Administrative Regulations or any official legal source.
False. The Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act was enacted in 1990 by the Nitijela, but the cited publication date and phrasing are inaccurate.
True. PacLII is the official publisher of Marshall Islands Supreme Court decisions, including the cited 2024 case.
False. The Marshall Islands Judiciary has not published any 2026 decision; future dates are impossible.
False. The Constitution is a foundational legal instrument, not an administrative regulation, and cannot be published in the 2025 Marshall Islands Administrative Regulations.
False. The Marshall Islands has no published 2025 judicial decisions; the claimed case and date are anachronistic and unverifiable.
False. The Marshall Islands has no connection to Australia's Federal Register of Legislation, making this bibliographic claim implausible.
False. The Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act is a domestic statute, not an Australian legal source, and was not published by Open Australian Legal Corpus.
False. RONLAW is Nauru's database; Marshall Islands decisions are published on its own PacLII or official judiciary site, not RONLAW.
True. The Marshall Islands Judiciary is the official publisher of its own court decisions, including constitutional interpretations.
